statement.text:
Let G be a finite group with an abelian Sylow p-subgroup A. Suppose that
B is a strongly closed elementary abelian subgroup of A. Without invoking the
Classification Theorem for Finite Simple Groups (CFSG), prove that G has a normal
subgroup N such that B = Ω1 (A ∩ N ).
    For p = 2, this is a corollary of a theorem of Goldschmidt. For p odd, this has
been proved by Flores and Foote (Adv. Math., 222 (2009), 453–484), but their proof
relies on CFSG. A CFSG-free proof in the special case when p = 3 and A has 3-
rank 3 would already be quite interesting. This case arises in Aschbacher’s treatment
of the e(G) = 3 problem, and a proof would provide an alternative to part of his
argument. (For this application, one could assume that all proper simple sections of
G are known.)                                                             R. Solomon
